title: Taifa of Ronda
capsule: The Taifa of Ronda was a Berber Muslim kingdom in the western Andalusian highlands, ruled by the Yafranid (Banu Ifran) dynasty from their capital at Ronda. Founded around 1039–1040 after the collapse of the Caliphate of Córdoba, it passed through several rulers—Abu Nour, Badis ibn Hilal, and finally Abu Nars Fatuh—before the Abbadid ruler of Seville, Abbad II al-Mu'tadid, absorbed it around 1065–1066 as part of his campaign to consolidate the western taifas. The kingdom's mountainous terrain gave it a degree of natural resilience, but it lacked the resources to resist the expanding Abbadid power.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent is inferred from the capital at Ronda and surrounding mountain districts; no detailed boundary documentation survives for this minor taifa.
